function.name: evolve_creatures
function.description: Apply the Evolutionary Algorithm to improve the creatures in a simulation over generations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

population_size.description: The initial size of the creature population.

mutation_rate.description: The probability of mutation in each generation. This is a float type value.

generations.description: The number of generations to run the simulation.

fitness_goal.description: The fitness goal that the creatures should strive for. This is an optional parameter. Default: 1

message.content:
### Applying an Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) to Game AI *(A practical guide – from theory to implementation)* --- ## 1. Why Use an EA in Games? | Goal | Why an EA Helps | |------|----------------| | **Evolve complex behaviors** | Hand‑coding every nuance of a character’s decision tree is tedious; an EA can discover surprising tactics automatically. | | **Optimize hyper‑parameters** | Tune weights of a neural net, aggression levels, or path‑finding heuristics without manual tweaking. | | **Generate content** | Create varied maps, puzzles, or enemy layouts that adapt to player skill. | | **Adapt to players** | Continuously evolve NPCs that learn from human playstyles. | --- ## 2. Core Components of a Game‑AI EA | Component | What It Does | Typical Implementation | |-----------|--------------|------------------------| | **Genome / Chromosome** | Encodes a candidate solution (e.g., a set of weights, a sequence of actions). | • Binary string
• Real‑valued vector
• Tree (for behavior trees)
• Neural network weights | | **Population** | A collection of genomes evaluated each generation. | Size `N` (often 50–200). | | **Fitness Function** | Quantifies how good a genome is at the task. | • Win/loss ratio
• Score achieved
• Distance travelled
• Composite metrics | | **Selection** | Chooses parents based on fitness. | • Tournament selection
• Roulette wheel (fitness proportionate)
• Rank selection | | **Crossover (Recombination)** | Combines two parents to produce offspring. | • One‑point / two‑point crossover (binary)
• Arithmetic blend (real‑valued)
• Subtree exchange (behavior trees) | | **Mutation** | Introduces random changes to maintain diversity. | • Bit flip (binary)
• Gaussian perturbation (real)
• Node replacement (trees) | | **Replacement Strategy** | Decides which individuals survive to next generation. | • Generational (replace all)
• Steady‑state (replace few)
• Elitism (keep best) | | **Termination Condition** | Stops evolution. | • Fixed number of generations
• Fitness threshold reached
• No improvement after X generations | --- ## 3. Step‑by‑Step Workflow ```text 1. Define the problem & decide what you want to evolve. 2. Choose a suitable genome representation. 3. Implement the fitness evaluator (runs the game or a simulation). 4. Set EA parameters (population size, mutation rate, crossover rate, etc.). 5. Loop: a. Evaluate fitness of all genomes. b. Select parents. c. Produce offspring via crossover + mutation. d. Replace part/all of the population. e. Check termination condition. ``` --- ## 4. Example: Evolving a Simple “Seek” Behavior Suppose we want an NPC to chase a target while avoiding obstacles. | Genome | Meaning | |--------|---------| | `[w1, w2, w3]` | Weights for three steering forces:
• `w1`: attraction to target
• `w2`: repulsion from obstacles
• `w3`: velocity smoothing | ### Fitness Function ```python def evaluate(genome): # Run a short simulation with this weight set score = 0 for step in range(SIM_STEPS): # Compute steering forces f_target = attract_to_target(target_pos) * genome[0] f_obstacle = avoid_obstacles(obstacle_list) * genome[1] f_smooth = smooth_velocity(current_vel) * genome[2] # Update velocity & position current_vel += f_target + f_obstacle + f_smooth current_pos += current_vel # Reward proximity to target dist = distance(current_pos, target_pos) score -= dist # Penalize collisions if collided_with_obstacle(current_pos): score -= COLLISION_PENALTY return -score # lower distance -> higher fitness ``` ### EA Parameters ```python population_size = 100 mutation_rate = 0.05 crossover_rate = 0.7 generations = 200 ``` ### Running the EA ```python from functions import evolve_creatures result = evolve_creatures({ "population_size": population_size, "mutation_rate": mutation_rate, "generations": generations, # fitness_goal omitted → defaults to 1 }) print(result.best_genome) # Best weight set found ``` *(In practice you’d replace the placeholder `evolve_creatures` with your own implementation.)* --- ## 5. Practical Tips & Common Pitfalls | Tip | Explanation | |-----|-------------| | **Keep simulations fast** | EA requires many evaluations; use simplified physics or shorter runs. | | **Use elitism sparingly** | Preserve the best but allow room for new ideas. | | **Normalize fitness** | If scores vary widely, scale them to avoid premature convergence. | | **Avoid over‑fitting** | Test evolved agents against unseen scenarios or random seeds. | | **Hybridize** | Combine EA with reinforcement learning (e.g., evolve NN weights then fine‑tune with RL). | | **Visualise progress** | Plot fitness curves to spot stagnation early. | --- ## 6. Advanced Variants | Variant | When to Use | |---------|-------------| | **Neuroevolution** | Evolve neural network weights or architectures directly. | | **Genetic Programming** | Evolve symbolic programs (e.g., Lisp‑style trees) for flexible behavior. | | **Co‑evolution** | Simultaneously evolve opponents or teammates. | | **Multi‑objective EA** | Optimize several goals simultaneously (speed vs. stealth). | | **Self‑adaptive parameters** | Let mutation/crossover rates evolve too. | --- ## 7. Resources | Resource | Type | Link | |----------|------|------| | *“An Introduction to Genetic Algorithms”* | Book | https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~dga/ | | *DEAP* | Python library | https://deap.readthedocs.io/ | | *OpenAI Gym* | Benchmark environments | https://gym.openai.com/ | | *Unity ML‑Agents* | Unity integration | https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ml-agents | | *Evolutionary Computation in Games* (research paper) | PDF | https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.04571.pdf | --- ## 8. Quick Checklist Before You Start 1. **Define clear objectives** – what success looks like. 2. **Choose a compact genome** – fewer genes → faster evolution. 3. **Implement a robust simulator** – accurate enough to reflect real gameplay. 4. **Set realistic EA parameters** – start with defaults, then tune. 5. **Validate results** – test evolved agents in diverse conditions. --- ### Bottom Line By treating game AI as an optimization problem, an evolutionary algorithm lets you let the system *discover* effective strategies, tune parameters, or generate content autonomously. With a solid fitness function, efficient simulation, and careful parameter tuning, EA can become a powerful tool in your game‑development toolkit. Happy evolving!
